title: Do plumbing and drainage work to the plumbing code (NCC Volume Three)
what: Carry out plumbing and drainage work to the Plumbing Code (NCC Volume Three) and the Code of Practice for Wastewater Management, which the regulations apply to all buildings and building work; the wastewater code prevails where the two conflict. The edition in force is NCC 2022; the Territory has not adopted NCC 2025. Its schedule in NCC 2025 varies 5 national provisions.

sources.title: Building Regulations 1993 (NT)
sources.quote: 4 Building Code and other codes adopted (1) Subject to these Regulations, the following apply to any building that can be classified according to use under Part A6 of the Building Code and to any building work referred to in the Act or in the Building Code: (a) the Building Code; (b) the Plumbing Code; (c) the Code of Practice for Wastewater Management.

sources.title: Building Regulations 1993 (NT)
sources.quote: Plumbing Code means the Plumbing Code of Australia set out in Volume Three of the National Construction Code.

administration.note: For plumbing and drainage done as part of building work under a building permit.

sources.title: Building Act 1993 (NT)
sources.locator: s 72B(1), words naming the body (found 27 Nov 2026) (current reprint)
sources.quote: 72B Granting certificate of substantial compliance (1) A building certifier must not grant a certificate of substantial compliance in relation to building work unless: (a) the certificate applies to a building of a class prescribed for section 72A(2)(a); and (b) the building, or the part of the building to which the certificate applies, is suitable for occupation; and (c) the building work meets the relevant technical standards;

triggers.note: when carrying out plumbing or drainage work

reach.note: Volume Three, the Plumbing Code of Australia, covers plumbing and drainage work.

sources.title: Building Regulations 1993 (NT)
sources.quote: 4 Building Code and other codes adopted (1) Subject to these Regulations, the following apply to any building that can be classified according to use under Part A6 of the Building Code and to any building work referred to in the Act or in the Building Code: (a) the Building Code; (b) the Plumbing Code; (c) the Code of Practice for Wastewater Management.

confidence_note: The law's own words require building or plumbing work to comply with the code. Drafted on 27 November 2026 for the NCC work (docs/plan_ncc_ingestion.md, phase N3); the variation counts are from the NCC 2025 dataset.

assessment.summary: Work must meet the National Construction Code (Volume Three, the Plumbing Code of Australia) as the Northern Territory applies it. The code sets minimum safety, health, amenity, accessibility and energy standards, whose benefits are not weighed here; meeting and certifying them adds to the cost of every project.

marks.reason: Designing, documenting and certifying each project against the code adds cost, and the state's own variations add to it for builders who work in several states.

assessment.confidence_note: Marked to agree with the NCC adoption records (burden -1); the Productivity Commission finds several code changes were adopted although their impact analyses showed a net cost. No evaluation of the requirement itself was found.
